$comment: Copy to <project>/.claude/framework-manifest.json at install and fill it in. SETUP.md step 7 walks this.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The install RENAMES most of what it copies: stacks/<name>/ becomes
docs/stack-backend/, modules/contracts/ becomes docs/contracts/, tooling/gate/gate-<stack>.sh becomes
gate.sh at each repo root, tooling/ci/gate.yml becomes .github/workflows/gate.yml. Nothing recorded those
renames, so /framework-upgrade could only resolve docs/process/ -- the one directory whose mapping is 1:1.
For everything else it had no way to know which upstream file an installed file came from, and the stack
identity was destroyed outright: once stacks/dotnet-api/ is called docs/stack-backend/, nothing on disk
says it was dotnet-api. The upgrade silently skipped layer 2, the review templates, the gate scripts and
CI -- which is where all the editable content lives.
This file is the record. Every entry is one installed artifact and the upstream path it came from, so the
upgrade has a resolvable source for every target, /framework-doctor has a real layout check, and the
CHANGELOG's prose mapping table stops being load-bearing.
KEEP IT CURRENT. It is written at install and updated by /framework-upgrade. If you add a stack, add a
repo, or install an optional module later, add its entries here at the same time -- an entry that is
missing is a file the upgrade will not see.
$comment_answers: The SETUP answers that decide which files are installed and which rules apply. /framework-doctor reads these; keep them identical to the matching lines in CLAUDE.md.
$comment_stacks: The upstream stacks/<name>/ folder behind each installed docs/stack-*/ directory. Without this the upgrade cannot tell which stack a project installed, because the install renamed the folder. Delete the slot a project does not use rather than leaving it blank.
$comment_repos: Repo-root-relative artifacts are installed once PER REPO. Single-repo projects list one entry with an empty path.
$comment_class: class matches the CHANGELOG's upgrade actions and decides what an upgrade may do without asking:
copy    layer 1/2 doc. The project never edits it, so replace outright. Drift here is a finding.
merge   the project edited this at install (gate commands, filled placeholders). NEVER overwrite;
the upgrade quotes the upstream change for a human to apply.
local   generated at install from a template and owned by the project from then on. The upgrade
reports upstream changes but does not touch the file.
$comment_omitted: Delete every entry above that this project did not install -- an optional module it skipped, a second
stack it does not have, the .ps1 gates on a POSIX-only team. A manifest that claims files which are not
